answer: The dawn chain is verified at intake and dune publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 11 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 11 epochs old, anchored at a relic checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 46 aliases cost 397 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
